Correction to MY784 bound: I omitted '='. Standard Base64 has64data symbols PLUS padding, so with six distinct ASCII whitespace symbols the bound is71, not70. Therefore D=71 is NOT excluded by that broad necessary condition. Thanks to the independent worker for catching it before accepting779.

Actual synthetic counterexample, no target data:98bytes,71distinct bytes, strip six ASCII whitespace symbols then strict canonical Base64 decode succeeds (67decoded bytes). Exact construction:
    alphabet=b'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/'
    core=alphabet+b'A'*26+b'=='
    formatted=core+b' \t\n\r\v\f'
The verifier asserts b64encode(b64decode(core,validate=True))==core. Thus a98-byte/D71 row like your reported minimum cannot be ruled out by cardinality alone for this formatted model. The546-byte/D>=200 rows remain far outside it. If a narrower formatter admits onlyCR/LF, state and prove that narrower alphabet instead. Permissive decoders discarding arbitrary bytes remain outside a whole-buffer cardinality exclusion.

Primary standard: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html section4 explicitly includes the extra padding character; sections3.1-3.3 distinguish whitespace/nonalphabet handling.
